anchorOrder: LINEAR, 014-style through 019, and in this order: (1) harness/STUDY-MANIFEST.sha256 covers the registered documents, the artifacts and the code, and covers NEITHER itself NOR this file; (2) this file pins that manifest's digest in studyManifest.sha256; (3) the freeze commit anchors this file. Study 014's round 3 established this order after round 2 built a cycle - the manifest hashing PINS.json while PINS.json stored the manifest's digest - which cannot be initialized without finding a SHA-256 fixed point. Each link is fillable in one pass, and after the freeze harness/make_manifest.py can still rewrite the manifest but cannot rewrite the digest pinned here. DEVIATIONS.md, README.md, PREREG-REVIEW.md, CORRECTION-TARGETS.md and harness/ADVISORIES.md are outside the manifest by construction (ADR 0004, PREREGISTRATION.md section 4b and section 7 delta 11), so a post-freeze deviation entry, a review round and an advisory all break no anchor.

batch.note: PORT CARRY AT STUDY 019's ROUND COUNT, AND NOT YET A STUDY 020 REGISTRATION. PREREGISTRATION.md §2.1 registers the compute condition — the codex.reasoningEffort value AND the per-arm N together — as an OUTPUT of the pre-pilot effort sweep, and §2 carries a TODO(prereg) for the re-derived call order, the attained position spread and the re-pinned batch.order / batch.n / batch.slots. §7 delta 7 has landed the DERIVATION: harness/batch.py holds no round count of its own and reads this block, derive_order(rounds) is the authority at any N, schedule() asserts the expansion attains the spreads PUBLISHED here rather than 019's (1, 1), and harness/tests/test_schedule.py re-runs the search at whatever round count this block names. The numbers below are Study 019's, independently re-derived by that search at 50 rounds and carried so the ported driver runs; re-pinning at the swept N is `batch.py derive-schedule --rounds N` plus an edit of this block, and no constant in batch.py moves. Sequential, never parallel. The per-call timeout ceiling is an APPARATUS bound: a call that reaches it is pipeline-invalid, excluded from every rate's denominator and reported with its own rate, and a per-arm timeout rate above timeoutRateCap is a control-gate failure adjudicating R1 in neither direction. The wrapper reads callTimeoutSeconds and timeoutKillAfterSeconds from HERE, so the registry, the driver and the wrapper cannot hold three ceilings; a harness test asserts these two values equal batch.py's constants.

order.construction: W1-W3 increment every symbol A->B->C->A per row; W4-W6 are those rows reversed
order.derivedBy: harness/batch.py derive_order(rounds=50), exhaustively over the 720 orderings of W1-W6 and the 30 ordered two-sequence tails, keeping the orders in which no arm ever immediately follows itself and returning the lexicographically-least of those minimizing (position spread, transition spread). The spreads above are what that search ATTAINED at this round count; §7 delta 7 publishes them because 019 asserted the pair (1, 1) as a floor, which is true at 50 rounds and wrong by construction at any other N.
order.note: 50 rounds of three arms: eight whole blocks of the six Williams sequences and a two-sequence tail, because 50 is not a multiple of 6. Exact balance is arithmetically unavailable at three arms over 50 rounds - 50 slots do not divide over 3 positions and 149 transitions do not divide over 6 ordered pairs - so what the search attains is position spread 1 and directed-transition spread 1, with no arm ever immediately following itself. Those attained values are published above as data; harness/batch.py's schedule() requires the expansion to attain them EXACTLY, so a drifted order fails and a stale registry fails too, and harness/tests/test_schedule.py re-runs the search rather than trusting this cache.

codex.note: The binary digest and the CLI version carry from Study 019, where 019's values still govern the same executable; they are design-time-resolved and are enforced under both labels. The MODEL and the REASONING EFFORT are null and are NOT freeze pins: ruling M-25 registers them as DESIGN-TIME-RESOLVED pins whose value the pre-pilot effort sweep produces (section 2.1), and a value the pre-freeze sweep must produce cannot be a value the freeze fills. A null in either one still labels the run PILOT - integrity.study_label() reads DESIGN_TIME_PINS beside FREEZE_PINS - with ONE registered exemption, one value and one label wide: under the --sweep label reasoningEffort alone is exempt, because the sweep is the procedure that resolves it and a gate that refuses the sweep forbids its own input. harness/authoring_call.sh refuses while model is null rather than passing the string None to -m. model and reasoningEffort are design-time-resolved pins, NOT freeze pins: neither is in integrity.FREEZE_PINS, and what a null one does is refuse the CALL under both labels while still labelling the run PILOT through DESIGN_TIME_PINS. M-24, stated rather than glossed: there is no transcript witness to bind the effort to today - 019's session.jsonl carries one turn_context naming model and no effort member - so unless the witness-resolution step at pin time finds one, this pin is a CALL.json SELF-REPORT WHERE NO TRANSCRIPT WITNESS EXISTS. A pin nobody can check is a recorded intention, and that sentence travels with every published record of the condition.
codex.reasoningEffortFlagProvenance: RESOLVED EMPIRICALLY 2026-08-24 against the pinned binary (binarySha256 above, codex-cli 0.145.0), with NO model call. codex exec --help names no reasoning-effort flag of any spelling - the count of lines mentioning 'effort' in that help is zero - so the flag PREREGISTRATION.md section 2.1 registers as resolved at pin time does not exist as a flag. The only spelling this build accepts is the config override -c model_reasoning_effort=<tier>: -c is the argv flag (reasoningEffortFlag) and model_reasoning_effort is a ConfigToml field of this build (reasoningEffortConfigKey). The two members are separate because the wrapper's seat emits FLAG then VALUE, and a config override's value is KEY=VALUE - collapsing them into one member would either hard-code the key in the shell, which section 2.1 forbids, or send the bare tier after -c, which this build would read as a malformed override. harness/authoring_call.sh composes the pair from these two members and stamps both into CALL.json.
codex.reasoningEffortNote: M-24, ruled as drafted. The wrapper passes this value by explicit flag and stamps it into every CALL.json. THERE MAY BE NO TRANSCRIPT WITNESS TO BIND IT TO: 019's session.jsonl carries exactly one turn_context record whose payload names model and no effort member, and the only occurrence of reasoning_effort anywhere is an override slot holding null. A witness-resolution step sets the flag and inspects the resulting session.jsonl for a non-null member naming the effort. If one exists, transcript gate 5 is extended to it with the same turn-context-mismatch reason tag and the same apparatus-side classification. If none exists, this pin is registered as a CALL.json self-report where no transcript witness exists, with reasoning_output_tokens entering C4 as a band - a pin nobody can check is a recorded intention, and the preregistration says so. THE FLAG'S SPELLING HALF OF THAT TODO IS CLOSED (2026-08-24, see reasoningEffortFlagProvenance): the pinned CLI has no reasoning-effort flag and the spelling is the config override -c model_reasoning_effort=<tier>. THE WITNESS HALF IS OPEN and is resolved as the SWEEP'S STEP ZERO rather than by an extra probe: harness/batch.py's sweep subcommand inspects the FIRST sweep call's own session.jsonl, decides the branch on turn_context alone (transcript gate 5 is a turn_context gate; a non-null occurrence in another record type is published and does not decide it), and records the branch into SWEEP.json. The branch then lands here in reasoningEffortWitness, and the corresponding change to harness/transcript_check.py lands with it - the sweep publishes the branch, it does not amend the gate.

registeredLabelRule: harness/integrity.py's study_label() labels a run REGISTERED only when EVERY pin the rule reads is filled, and the rule reads TWO tuples. FREEZE_PINS, eighteen members: preregistration, policyProse, goldSuite, the three arm prompt digests (matrixA/matrixB/matrixC, stored at arms.<ARM>.promptSha256, the member the call wrapper's prompt-digest gate reads), mutantManifests, referenceA, referenceB, offGoldCertificate, studyManifest, opa.capabilitiesSha256 (opaCapabilities), jpack.reproducibleBuildAttestation (jpackBuildAttestation), probePrompt.sha256 (probePrompt), golden.sha256 (goldenContext), isolationNegative.assent (isolationAssent) reviewerMutantSet.sha256 (reviewerMutantSet) and censusStimulus.count (censusStimulusCount), the last of which is new in 020 because section 5.1's E5 registers the census count as freeze-pinned and Study 019 registered the same stimulus while pinning no count. DESIGN_TIME_PINS, two members and NEW IN 020 under ruling M-25: codex.model (model) and codex.reasoningEffort (reasoningEffort). Study 019 carried codex.model as a freeze pin; it moves here because the compute condition is an OUTPUT of the pre-pilot sweep, which runs before the freeze, and a value the pre-freeze sweep must produce cannot be a value the freeze fills. The move is not a relaxation: a null in either design-time pin labels the run PILOT exactly as a null freeze pin does, and a PILOT supports no claim. The non-null members are enforced under both labels: a design-time resolved toolchain digest is checked whether or not the freeze has happened. ONE exemption is registered, one value and one label wide: under the --sweep label codex.reasoningEffort ALONE is exempt from the null check, because the sweep is the registered procedure that resolves it; codex.model is never exempt, every sweep call stamps its setting into its own CALL.json, and the sweep's outputs are citable: false and outside every population. harness/tests/test_pins.py drives the rule pin by pin: each member nulled alone on an otherwise-full registry must produce PILOT, and the sweep exemption must hold for exactly one pin and exactly one label. THE DESIGN-TIME HALF IS ALSO A GATE ON THE CALL, and it is a different rule with a different consequence: the pins section 2 marks resolvedAtDesignTime - codex.model, codex.reasoningEffort, codex.binarySha256, jpack.binarySha256, opa.assetSha256 - are checked WHETHER OR NOT THE FREEZE HAS HAPPENED, by harness/batch.py's require_design_time_pins(), which refuses the call rather than changing the label. codex.reasoningEffort ALONE is exempt under the --sweep label (harness/batch.py's SWEEP_EXEMPT_PINS and harness/integrity.py's SWEEP_EXEMPT_PINS name the same one member), the sweep still runs inside the harness, and nothing else is exempt at any label. NOTE, as a finding rather than a silence: Study 019 carried codex.model in FREEZE_PINS and section 2.1 rules it a design-time-resolved pin; ruling M-25 moves it, so it is in DESIGN_TIME_PINS and not in FREEZE_PINS here, and harness/tests/test_pins.py asserts the two tables do not overlap.

sweep.abortRule: A setting whose FIRST arm-A call exceeds the registered per-call ceiling (batch.callTimeoutSeconds) is aborted after that call; a setting whose per-arm mean duration projects a primary batch beyond 72 h at the registered N branch is recorded as out of budget and is not swept further. Aborted settings are published with the call that aborted them.
sweep.budgetProjectionNote: The abort rule's second clause projects a primary batch 'beyond 72 h at the registered N branch'. batch.n carries Study 019's round count as a PORT CARRY under section 7 delta 7 and is NOT YET a Study 020 registration - the per-arm N is an output of this sweep - so the driver projects at whatever batch.n holds and RECORDS which branch it used; over a registry with no count at all the projection falls to the ONE branch PREREGISTRATION.md section 2.1's dual-pricing table prices, N = 60/arm = 180 calls, which that table calls a priced illustration of one branch and not a registered N. When batch.n is filled the driver projects at THAT value instead and records which of the two it used; it never silently picks the cheaper one. budgetHours and budgetProjectionN are asserted equal to harness/batch.py's SWEEP_BUDGET_HOURS and SWEEP_BUDGET_PROJECTION_N by harness/tests/test_sweep.py.
sweep.note: PREREGISTRATION.md section 2.1, rulings M-8/M-20/M-25. The pre-pilot effort sweep is n = 3/arm across three settings, run THROUGH the registered apparatus (harness/authoring_call.sh + harness/batch.py under --sweep, never outside the harness - running it outside is the 019 failure exactly). Its outputs are citable: false and outside every population. The registered compute condition - the codex.reasoningEffort value and the per-arm N together - is chosen from its result and priced at its own observed durations. The cap is not raised without a DEVIATIONS.md entry naming the reason and republishing the price.
sweep.noteOnTheModesName: The mode section 2.1 calls '--sweep' is the driver SUBCOMMAND harness/batch.py sweep - the subcommand form every other mode of this driver takes (plan, run, capture, capture-golden, capture-isolation-negative, shortfall) - and PIN_LABEL=SWEEP is what that mode claims at the wrapper. The name is reconciled in PREREGISTRATION.md section 2.1 under 'Where the set is carried, and the mode's name'; nothing about the exemption's width moves with it, and the wrapper still accepts the label from the driver and from nowhere else.
sweep.publication: The prereg's published-in-full obligation is discharged by two files under sweep.root: SWEEP.json, the machine-readable ledger (every call's setting, arm, run index, duration, completion bytes, reasoning_output_tokens where the transcript carries it, wrapper exit and refusal code, plus the per-setting abort verdicts and the M-24 witness branch), and SWEEP.md, the rendered per-setting per-arm table. Both are written for ABORTED settings too, carrying the call that aborted them, and both stamp citable: false on every row.

sweep.settingsProvenance: Measured 2026-08-24 against the pinned binary with no model call. (1) codex exec --help names no reasoning-effort flag; the spelling is the config override recorded under codex.reasoningEffortFlag / codex.reasoningEffortConfigKey. (2) codex debug models renders this build's own model catalog offline: over its EIGHT models the tier vocabulary is low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra; low/medium/high/xhigh are supported by 8/8, max by 3/8 and ultra by 2/8. The swept set is the three LOWEST of the universally supported four, so it survives whichever model codex.model is pinned to. (3) Every model's own default_reasoning_level lies inside the set - low for gpt-5.6-sol, the model Study 019's batch ran, medium for the other seven - so the set contains the default 019's batch implicitly ran at and extends monotonically upward in cost. xhigh is as AVAILABLE as the three swept tiers, so its exclusion is a BUDGET decision and is registered as one, not passed off as an availability limit.
sweep.settingsUncapClause: xhigh, max and ultra are NOT swept and are reachable only by a DEVIATIONS.md entry naming the reason and republishing the price, under the same cap clause that governs raising callCap: reaching a costlier tier is the same act as buying more calls. harness/batch.py refuses a setting outside sweep.settings, and harness/authoring_call.sh refuses one too, so the deviation has to be written before either will run it.
